neighbours.label: Weak guess: talk about learners building skill and judging their own achievement (the pole's top peaks are scattered function words and verbs in such text)
fire: Great coaches help teenagers see how much their effort matters.
Many gifted pupils see their marks as proof of their value.
Daily drills make a beginner steadier on any instrument.
Mentors remind trainees to look at growth, not just scores.
Tutors encourage children to see their own mistakes as lessons.
Repetition makes a student faster at mental arithmetic.
Anxious learners see each exam as a verdict on themselves.
Workshops teach apprentices to judge their own craft, not just the result.
quiet: Great gardeners help teenagers plant how much their street needs.
Many old farmers sell their apples at the edge of their land.
Daily rain makes the river higher along any road.
Drivers remind tourists to look at the bridge, not the cliffs.
Nurses encourage visitors to wash their own hands at the door.
Salt makes a stew tastier on cold evenings.
Hungry goats eat each leaf on the hedge by the barn.
Shops sell tourists maps of their own city, and the bus times.
